item.title: 0.1.0-rc.2
item.description:
A color is copied from anywhere on the screen with Pick Color: that is the second release candidate.

Added

  • Pick Color, a command that shows the loupe of macOS to copy a color from anywhere on the screen: hex unless Settings → Color says another way. It needs no permission to see the screen. A card beside the pointer shows the color and says what was copied. A color a Display P3 screen shows beyond sRGB keeps what it is in OKLCH and the other wide ways, and hex and RGB say the nearest color they can.

item.title: 0.1.0-rc.1
item.description:
Files and contacts are found from the launcher, each with a command of its own, and modules have an index of their own to put what they know into the search: that is the first release candidate.

Added

  • Search Files, a command with a screen of its own: files and folders by name, with a preview of the selected one and what the Spotlight index knows about it. With nothing typed it lists what you opened lately. A menu, or Tab, narrows it down to folders, documents, images, videos, audio or code. Return opens a file, ⌘↵ shows it in Finder, ⌘C copies it and ⇧⌘C its path. What to search for can be typed along in the search, and the command can be chosen as a fallback.
  • Contacts: people and companies from your contacts are found in the search by name, nickname, company or email address. Return opens one in Contacts, ⌘↵ writes an email, and ⌘K lists the rest: message, call, copy. Inky reads your contacts only after you allowed it under Settings → Contacts, keeps them in memory, and writes nothing of them to disk. A contact that has a picture is shown by it.
  • Search Contacts, a command with a screen of its own: every contact by name, narrowed down to people, companies or one of your groups in a sidebar, with the numbers, addresses and birthday of the selected one and what can be done with it. Tab goes through the sidebar.
  • A search index for what is found without being a command, which modules, and later extensions, write their items to. Such items are ranked with everything else, but do not appear among the commands, and of each source only its best matches are listed.

Changed

  • Files are found by the words of their name in any order: “watcher folder” finds FolderWatcher.swift.
  • Looking files up no longer holds the launcher up. Asking Spotlight about the files it found took up to 50 ms a search, during which nothing typed was shown.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.6
item.description:
Copying a long text or a large image, and installing an application, no longer hold Inky up: that is the sixth alpha.

Changed

  • Copying a long text no longer holds Inky up. Before, a text of a few megabytes was gone through in full to tell whether it was code, which took up to seconds, also while Inky was in the background. The clipboard history no longer tells code apart: what was listed as code is listed as text, and found under Text as before.
  • Copying a large image no longer holds up the clipboard history while the image is kept: it is written first, and searching and scrolling go on meanwhile.
  • An application that is installed or removed is found or gone within a few seconds, without the launcher having to be opened. Before, opening the launcher looked for applications again whenever it had not for half a minute.
  • The clipboard history shows the images in its list from a small copy made for them, which it draws many times as quickly as the copy the selected image is shown by. Images copied before keep being shown by that.
